knowledge_point.title: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+11z &=-1 \\ 2x+5y+27z &=-5.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 11 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 27 & -5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 11 & -1 \\ 2 & 5 & 27 & -5\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 11 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -3\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -3\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+z &=5 \\ y+5z &=-3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-z+5 \\ y &=-5z-3 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-z+5 \\ -5z-3 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+5z &=-6 \\ 2x-3y+9z &=-6.\end{aligned}\right.

The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 5 & -6 \\ 2 & -3 & 9 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$

$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+3z &=6 \\ y-z &=6.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and we have one free variable, $z$. That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-3z+6 \\ y &=z+6 \\ z &=z,\end{aligned}\right.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-3z+6 \\ z+6 \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y+z &=5 \\ 2x-2y+3z &=11.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & -2 & 3 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & -2 & 3 & 11\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y &=4 \\ z &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $z$, and we have one free variable, $y$. That means we need to find $x$ and $z$ in terms of $y$.

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=y+4 \\ y &=y \\ z &=1,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}y+4 \\ y \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
